sector: A two-person coastal distillery making small-batch gin and cask-strength single malt, sold shop-direct and through independent merchants.
founded_place_size: Founded 2020, on the Northumberland coast, England. A two-person distillery: Iris runs the still, her partner runs everything else.
about: Coble & Vane is a working distillery on a stretch of the North Sea coast, named for the flat-bottomed fishing boat that once beached below the still house. We release twelve casks a year and nothing we cannot stand behind. The bottle is meant to earn its place on a shelf and in a hand, not to shout across the shop.
audience: Buyers aged 30 to 55 choosing a gift or a considered bottle, and the independent merchant deciding whether the bottle earns its shelf facing. People who read a label closely and reward restraint.
price_positioning: Bottles 55 to 120 dollars: standard gin at 55, cask-strength single malt from 95 to 120. Upper-craft tier, sitting deliberately apart from the twelve-dollar shelf. Value is carried by finish, emboss and wax rather than by loud print.
typography: Display in an engraved-feeling serif with real weight in the caps, set with generous letter spacing. Text in a quiet humanist sans for supplier and label copy. The type stays out of the way and lets a single ink do the work.
voice: Plain, dry, unhurried. Written as instruction, not advertisement. Example line: "One ink, plenty of air, and nothing shiny. If our own list looks wrong to you, say so before you make it."
brand_assets_status: The house mark was drawn six years ago by an illustrator who has since moved abroad and cannot be reached. It survives only as a full-colour illustration flattened to a single PNG. There are no vector files, no one-ink versions, and no supplier guidance sheet. Every single-colour version a supplier has ever received was improvised from that one file, and no two have matched.
values: Restraint and honesty. One deep ink, generous clear space, and finishes that carry the value instead of the print. Say plainly what a version can and cannot do.
